sections.h2: Where do Surry County property tax questions go?
sections.html:
To the Tax Department at the Surry County Service Center, 915 East Atkins Street, Dobson, North Carolina 27017. The phone is (336) 401-8100, and hours are 8:15 am to 5:00 pm Monday through Friday.

Assessment and collections use separate mailing boxes: P.O. Box 588 for assessment and P.O. Box 576 for collections. The department also takes payments at a drive-thru window at the same address, and an online taxpayer portal handles bill searches.

sections.h2: How is Surry County organized for tax appraisal?
sections.html:
Surry County has roughly 44,000 parcels, which the appraisal staff divides into about 370 neighborhoods built from similar market, economic and geographic conditions, such as a subdivision where homes share age, style and construction quality.

The county's own description of its revaluation covers four main steps: neighborhooding, pricing of land and buildings from sales data, field and office review, and mailing notices of assessment with an appeal review. Commissioners must approve the Schedule of Values before it takes effect, and that manual sets the rates and ranges the appraisers use.

sections.h2: When was the last Surry County revaluation?
sections.html:
The current revaluation took effect January 1, 2025. The county moved from the eight-year state maximum to a five-year cycle after a 2017 commissioners' vote, with a revaluation effective January 1, 2021, and then described itself as on a four-year cycle.

Notices of value for 2025 were mailed in February 2025. Values stay in place until the next revaluation, except for changes in the property itself. Ask the Tax Department for the date of the next cycle.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Surry County value?
sections.html:
You can ask for an informal review by the Tax Department or file a formal appeal with the Board of Equalization and Review. Surry County appointed a special board in 1982 under G.S. 105-322, and it convenes each year by the first Monday in May.

  • Commissioners reappoint the board each January from county residents.
  • The board can change any value it finds in need of adjustment.
  • A timely appellant gets the chance to appear.
  • After the board votes, the next step is the North Carolina Property Tax Commission.

The county encourages you to bring documentation that shows why the assessed value does not match fair market value, or details about the property that affect value.

sections.h2: How do Surry County taxes get paid and when do they go delinquent?
sections.html:
The Collections Office collects real, personal and business property tax. Interest is added monthly to taxes paid on or after January 6, at 2% for the first month and three quarters of one percent for each month after, and the county says the tax and interest charges are not negotiable.

Surry County collection rules at a glance
TopicWhat the county page says
Interest startOn or after January 6 after the due date
Rate2% first month, 3/4% each month after
EnforcementGarnishment, bank attachment, seizure, foreclosure (G.S. 105-365 to 105-368)
Limit on real property remediesWithin 10 years of the due date (G.S. 105-378)

Surry County posts a delinquent real property taxpayer list on its collections page.

sections.h2: What does Surry County offer in property tax relief?
sections.html:
State programs apply here: the elderly or disabled exclusion (greater of $25,000 or 50% of value), the disabled veteran exclusion (first $45,000), and the circuit breaker deferment. Each is filed on form AV-9 with the county assessor, and an owner can receive only one.

The Tax Department's menu also lists a present use value program for farm and forest land. Call (336) 401-8100 to ask how to apply, and note that applications are generally accepted through June 1 of the tax year.

sections.h2: What should a Surry County seller know about taxes at closing?
sections.html:
A tax lien attaches to the parcel as of the date property is listed, so the current year's bill travels with the house until it is paid. A seller typically settles it from proceeds, with the closing attorney confirming the amount.

If a house has fallen behind, ask the Collections Office for the payoff before you accept an offer. Surry County runs a foreclosure map and delinquent list through its tax pages, and an as-is cash buyer can still close if the past-due amount is cleared at the table.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Surry County and how does that shape its tax base?
sections.html:
The county describes itself as in the foothills of North Carolina, part of the Piedmont Triad region, with a large agricultural economy and a varied industrial base. It sits on interstate access, in the Yadkin Valley Appellation, and draws visitors to attractions tied to Mayberry and to outdoor recreation.

Surry was formed in 1771 from Rowan County and once included land that is now Stokes, Forsyth and Yadkin counties. The Register of Deeds in Dobson still holds records back to that year. For owners, farmland matters: the Tax Department lists a present use value program alongside its assessment and personal property pages.

sections.h2: What did the Surry County revaluation FAQ say about how values are set?
sections.html:
The county defines revaluation as making sure each assessed value reflects fair market value, meaning the most probable price in a competitive and open market. It says the work is required by law, because property values do not all rise or fall at the same rate and, without periodic revaluation, some owners would pay more than their share.

The county's FAQ says the Schedule of Values includes adjustments for construction types and market conditions and valuation schedules for land, and that its rates stay in effect until the next revaluation. Improvements added in between are appraised under the same standards. Call (336) 401-8100 to talk with an appraiser at the Dobson office.

sections.h2: How does the circuit breaker work for a Surry County homeowner?
sections.html:
It limits tax to 4.0% of income if income is up to the eligibility limit, and 5.0% if income is above the limit and up to 150% of it. The state form prints $38,800 and $58,200 for the 2026 tax year, and a new application is needed every year.

The owner must be 65 or totally and permanently disabled, live in North Carolina and have owned and lived in the home as a permanent residence at least five years. The excess tax is deferred and becomes a lien, with the three preceding fiscal years of deferral coming due when the owner transfers the home, dies or stops using it as a residence. Applicants file with the county assessor.

sections.h2: What happens in a Surry County tax foreclosure?
sections.html:
The county can file a foreclosure action in the county where the land lies and serve the owner, spouse and other lienholders. The sale is a public auction, a commissioner can require a deposit of up to 20% of the bid, and the commissioner's fee can reach 5% of the purchase price.

Before confirmation, a person can redeem by paying all taxes, penalties, interest and costs. The county's tax pages carry a property tax foreclosures section, so check it and call (336) 401-8100 if your parcel has fallen behind. Settling the balance with a sale is often cheaper than letting it reach auction.

faqs.q: Where is the Surry County Tax Department?
faqs.a: 915 East Atkins Street, Dobson, NC 27017. It is open 8:15 am to 5:00 pm Monday through Friday.

faqs.q: When does Surry County charge interest on property taxes?
faqs.a: On taxes paid on or after January 6 following the due date: 2% for the first month and three quarters of one percent each month after.

faqs.q: When did the current Surry County revaluation take effect?
faqs.a: January 1, 2025. The county's prior revaluation took effect January 1, 2021.

faqs.q: When does the Surry County Board of Equalization and Review meet?
faqs.a: The board convenes each year by the first Monday in May to hear property tax appeals.

faqs.q: Can I pay Surry County taxes in person?
faqs.a: Yes. The Tax Department takes payments at a drive-thru window at 915 East Atkins Street in Dobson, and an online portal is available.
